Rapid revegetation and erosion control will be aided by including light seedings of quick emergence annuals such as barley or wheat in the mixture, and the use of appropriate fertilizer as indicated by soil tests. Drill seeding will be utilized where possible; inaccessible areas will be broadcast seeded.
Shrubs and trees will be planted in reclaimed areas. Optimal locations for such plantings are north slopes and drainageways. Precautions will be taken where necessary to prevent competition from grasses and forbs. This may include such measures as the use of scoria, sand, gravel or plastic aprons placed around individual seedlings. Westmoreland Resources has initiated a program for the collection of seed from native trees and shrubs for the development of seedlings to be used in reclamation.
Vegetative sampling will be conducted annually in reclaimed areas so that the progress of revegetation can be quantitively evaluated. Parameters to be measured will include canopy coverage, height growth, herbage yield and percent of survival (woody species). This information will provide a basis for comparing different reclamation treatments so that in future work the most successful procedures can be utilized.
Optimal and timely revegetation will allow the earliest possible return to the original use of disturbed land for crops, lifestock, wildlife, forests and recreation. This will significantly mitigate short-and-long-term impacts of mining the land.
